title: Linux permissions: making access intentional
objectives: Explain how owners, groups, and permission bits control Linux file access.
Identify an unnecessarily broad permission and explain its security impact.

learningObjectives.statement: Explain how owners, groups, and permission bits control Linux file access.
Identify an unnecessarily broad permission and explain its security impact.

body.value: Linux permissions answer a practical question: which identity may perform which action on a resource? Start by identifying the owner and group, then check whether the requested access is necessary for the task.
A permission that is convenient but broader than the job requires is a security finding, even when no incident has happened yet.
This lesson uses the same reasoning pattern that appears later in IAM reviews: identify the principal, identify the resource, identify the action, and reduce access to the smallest justified scope.
